customer_name: Woodpecker Home Repair (啄木鸟家庭维修)
business_problem: Woodpecker's large home-repair platform was generating too many alerts and too much fragmented observability data for human-only troubleshooting. Root-cause analysis depended on experience, self-built AI explorations were unstable, and engineering teams had to lean on operations staff for even routine diagnosis.
solution_summary: Woodpecker adopted Alibaba Cloud STAROps and Cloud Monitor 2.0 to build a unified intelligent-operations analysis platform for its national home-services business. STAROps uses UModel-style observability context and large-model reasoning so engineers can investigate incidents through natural-language queries instead of stitching together logs and alerts manually. The company embedded STAROps into its internal operations platform through APIs, which lets developers run first-line data queries and root-cause analysis without logging into Alibaba Cloud consoles or waiting for the operations team. To reduce alert noise, Woodpecker also configured long-running tasks that summarize critical incidents and push them to the right owner so key issues are not buried by low-value alarms. The result is a more self-service incident workflow in which platform data, diagnosis, and remediation guidance are available through one AI-assisted interface.

solution_components.name: STAROps
solution_components.role: Performs natural-language diagnosis, root-cause analysis, and repair suggestion generation for operations incidents.

solution_components.name: Cloud Monitor 2.0
solution_components.role: Unifies metrics, traces, and logs as the observability base for AI-driven operations analysis.

data_flow: Metrics, traces, and logs are unified in Cloud Monitor 2.0 and then consumed by STAROps for conversational diagnosis. STAROps returns likely root causes and repair suggestions, while API embedding sends the same analysis into Woodpecker's internal operations platform for developers and operators.
business_outcome: Woodpecker reduced the time and coordination needed to handle incidents across its platform. Teams can now use AI-assisted diagnostics directly inside their own operations environment, operations tickets are lower, and critical alerts are less likely to be lost in alert storms.
architecture_clues: STAROps is embedded into the customer's own platform by API so diagnosis can be delegated closer to developers.
Long-running alert missions are used to summarize critical incidents rather than only responding to one alert at a time.
The platform unifies metrics, traces, and logs before AI diagnosis instead of letting each data source remain siloed.
